text:
Jessica: ACME support reported a spike of streaming requests marked as 5xx. Customer insists their VSCode extension client closed the window mid-stream (so client-abort). Sample x-request-id=rid_acme_20240317. Can we triage?

Raj: please paste server logs + request headers and SDK/lang info.

Jessica: server log (trimmed):
```
2024-03-17T14:21:03.512Z router=gw-12 req=rid_acme_20240317 upstream=backend-9 status=200 latency=120ms
2024-03-17T14:21:03.634Z proxy=proxy-1 req=rid_acme_20240317 write_err="write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.1.2.3:54321: write: broken pipe"
2024-03-17T14:21:03.635Z router=gw-12 req=rid_acme_20240317 classify=result=5xx reason="proxy write failure"
```
request headers (sanitized):
```
:method: POST
:scheme: https
:authority: api.redwood.ai
content-type: application/octet-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
user-agent: vscode-extension/1.2.3
x-request-id: rid_acme_20240317
```
Client says they used fetch() inside VSCode extension and user closed the tab -> stream aborted.

Mike: router log shows upstream status=200; proxy write failed after that. Right now our pipeline maps many write errors to 5xx.

Emma: finance flagged this - customers are disputing charges because aborted streams were billed as 5xx retries. We need precise criteria to reclassify and a list of affected requests for credits.

Raj: quick trace query examples:
```
select req, upstream_status, proxy_err from traces where service='streaming-gateway' and proxy_err is not null limit 5;
-- rid_acme_20240317, 200, "broken pipe"
-- rid_xyz_20240316, 200, "write: broken pipe"
-- rid_foo_20240315, 502, "upstream reset"
```
So some are genuine upstream failures, others look like client exits mid-stream.

Mike: hypothesize half-close race: client FIN races with gateway writing final chunk -> proxy write returns EPIPE and we currently classify it as upstream 5xx. Need to distinguish client-initiated close vs upstream error. Can we get tcpdump for a sample?

Jessica: customer agreed. tcpdump snippet:
```
14:21:03.600 IP client -> gw FIN
14:21:03.601 IP gw -> backend PSH, ACK (sending last chunk)
14:21:03.634 RST from gw -> client
```
FIN arrives just before gateway writes trailer.

Mike: confirms race. Proposed short-term fix: change classification heuristic so that if we observe a client FIN within 250ms of proxy write failure, mark as client abort (no 5xx). Long-term: improve proxy to differentiate EPIPE vs upstream EOF and make write path recoverable; ensure proper chunked trailer handling.

Support-bot: alert suppression enabled for this error class to cut noise.

Emma: for billing we need CSV of requests in last 30 days where proxy_err ILIKE '%broken pipe%' and upstream_status=200 and client_ip not in allowlist. Can engineering produce?

Raj: generating now. Uploading secure CSV to S3 for finance + account team.

Raj: upload complete -> s3://redwood-support/acme/streaming_client_abort_matches_mar2024.csv (412 rows).

Mike: dev plan: open runtime PR with a feature flag. Behavior: on proxy write failure, if observed_client_fin_within(250ms) -> mark client_abort; else -> mark upstream_error. Add metric proxy.write_ePIPE_classified_client_abort. Will gate rollouts per customer/region.

Jessica: customer workaround suggestions: have client set Connection: close on cancellation or perform an explicit cancel API call before closing UI. Customer says VSCode extension can't easily change behavior today.

Mike: QA: create harness to inject client FIN at different offsets relative to chunk writes and validate classification toggles. Use socat/python to simulate.

Raj: test notes - backend: simple server that streams chunks; client: sleep then close socket to simulate user closing. Script attached to thread.

Ops-bot: deploy PR#8421 to staging canary at 02:00 UTC (gate-flagged).

Emma: finance will hold disputed charges for rows in CSV until PM confirms final classification.

Jessica: customer notified of temporary credit and planned fix. They appreciated quick response.

Mike: I'll follow up with short postmortem after rollout and confirm metrics (reduction in misclassified write errors).

Emma: please include exact CSV rows in PM so billing reconciliation is straightforward.

Jessica: closing loop once PR merged and finance confirms credits. Thanks all.
